items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] That’s so interesting. I mean you think about guys like — was it Neal Hefti who wrote “Batman?” ... And you guys were probably laughing when you were doing this “hefty/hefty/hefty.”

ctx.x: met Charlie Morrow, was one of the clients at Record Plant, and he had like an event business and he also did jingles. He was kind of on the fringe of the jingle industry. And one day we were just talking about synthesis and the future of how that’s going, and that and computer music, and where that is all going to, and he said, “oh I’ve got this jingle project, do you want to work on it with me?” And it was like kind of just doing a video version of the sounder for 10-10 WINS. But it was fun. And then he said,…

That’s so interesting. I mean you think about guys like — was it Neal Hefti who wrote “Batman?” And you know, probably the quickest thing he ever wrote and he probably made more money off that than the great Basie charts and all that stuff. And you guys were probably laughing when you were doing this “hefty/hefty/hefty.”

Oh yeah, we had a great time. Charlie was shorter than me so to do that I had him stand on a chair so we’d be like the same height on the mic, and slowed down the tape machine to do the “wimpys” and then sped it back up. And you know, I knew all the recording tricks. I knew all the production stuff. Plus I knew the music. So it worked really well. Like I wasn’t the best player in the world, I wasn’t the best engineer, but I did everything really, really well. So I could just go in and take care of any situation.
